# F-Droid metadata

App listings for the [F-Droid](https://f-droid.org) repository that publishes
this project's two Android apps, so they can be installed and updated from a
phone instead of being sideloaded with `adb install`.

```
metadata/com.lunchboxos.companion.yml
metadata/com.lunchboxos.companion/en-US/icon.png
metadata/com.lunchboxos.media.yml
metadata/com.lunchboxos.media/en-US/icon.png
```

## Who reads these files

**This repository's release job.** `release.yml` builds the repository at
<https://fdroid.lunchbox-os.com/fdroid/repo> from the release's APKs, the APKs
of every earlier release since v0.6.0, and these files at the release tag, then
uploads it to the R2 bucket behind that address. See
[`docs/release-signing.md`](../../docs/release-signing.md#the-f-droid-index-key)
for the key and the bucket, and
[`2026-09-29 1940 self-hosted-fdroid-repo (#205).md`](../../docs/ai/history/2026-09-29%201940%20self-hosted-fdroid-repo%20(%23205).md)
for why it is hosted this way.

Generating the repository is
[`scripts/ci/fdroid-update.sh`](../../scripts/ci/fdroid-update.sh), and three
things run it: the release's `publish` job, with the real index key; the
release's `apk` job, which validates each signed APK against these files with
a throwaway key before anyone approves the release; and
`lunchbox package fdroid`, which does the same locally (below).

Before 2026-09, the repository was generated by a service in the
[`fahrengit-451`](https://github.com/aarmea/fahrengit-451) stack on
`git.armeafamily.com`, from Forgejo releases. That is the design in
[`2026-07-26 002 fdroid-repository.md`](../../docs/ai/history/2026-07-26%20002%20fdroid-repository.md)
and [`003 fdroid-fahrengit-451-spec.md`](../../docs/ai/history/2026-07-26%20003%20fdroid-fahrengit-451-spec.md).

## Conventions

- **No version fields.** `fdroid update` reads `versionCode` and `versionName`
  out of the APK, so the repo-root `VERSION` stays the single source of truth and
  there is nothing here for `lunchbox version check` to police.
- **`AllowedAPKSigningKeys` pins the release certificate.** `fdroid update`
  refuses to publish an APK signed by any other key. Every release re-signs
  every earlier release's APKs into a new index, whether they came from the
  bucket or from release assets, so this is the control that stops a
  wrongly-signed APK from reaching a family device as an in-place upgrade. It
  must be updated if the release signing key ever changes:

  ```sh
  apksigner verify --print-certs lunchbox-companion_X.Y.Z.apk | grep 'SHA-256 digest'
  ```

- **One file per `applicationId`**, named exactly after it.
- **Each listing's icon is `<applicationId>/en-US/icon.png`**, a symlink to the
  app's artwork in [`assets/branding/icon/apps/`](../../assets/branding/icon/apps/).
  fdroidserver 2.x no longer extracts icons from the APK, so without it the
  client shows a placeholder. The repository's own icon is
  `assets/branding/icon/lunchbox-256.png`.

## Testing changes locally

```sh
sudo apt install --no-install-recommends fdroidserver default-jdk-headless
./scripts/lunchbox package fdroid --debug-keys   # after building APKs
```

`--no-install-recommends` matters: it takes the dependency tree from ~269
packages / ~300 MB to ~67 / ~78 MB (matplotlib and tk arrive as Recommends of
androguard and are not needed). `default-jdk-headless` matters because
fdroidserver signs the index with `/usr/lib/jvm/default-java/bin/jarsigner` and
prefers that path over every other JDK on the machine — if the default is a JRE,
the run fails at the very end with an opaque `OSError`.

`--debug-keys` drops the signing-key pin, which debug-signed local builds would
otherwise fail. Omit it when validating real release APKs. The generated repo
lands in `dist/fdroid-repo/` and can be served with any static file server to try
it on a phone:

```sh
python3 -m http.server -d dist/fdroid-repo 8080
# then add http://<host>:8080/repo in the F-Droid client
```
